However, since you are requesting aggregate statistics (counts per sex) rather than individual-level records, and your question can be fully answered with such aggregate counts, this is appropriately handled as a statistics request rather than requiring patient-level records.

notes: Interpreted 'at least one' and 'two or more' inpatient stays as EncounterCriterion min_count in each metric's where, counting distinct patients, grouped by sex.

runs.sql:
SELECT p.patient_id AS unit_id,
       p.patient_id,
       p.sex AS g0,
       ((SELECT count(*) FROM encounters x WHERE (x.patient_id = p.patient_id) AND (x.type IN ('inpatient')) AND (x.start_date >= DATE '2023-01-01') AND (x.start_date <= DATE '2025-12-31')) >= 1) AS m0_in,
       ((SELECT count(*) FROM encounters x WHERE (x.patient_id = p.patient_id) AND (x.type IN ('inpatient')) AND (x.start_date >= DATE '2023-01-01') AND (x.start_date <= DATE '2025-12-31')) >= 2) AS m1_in
FROM patients p
WHERE TRUE

assessment.explanation_for_applicant: Your purpose, planning emergency department capacity, is allowed under Art. 53 as a public health/policy-making activity. Since your question can be fully answered with aggregated counts per hospital and year, you only need anonymised statistics, not individual-level records, so this is granted as a statistics request.

notes: Hospital = data_holder; year = start_date year via start_year group_by, restricted to 2023-2025.
Distinct patients metric counts unique patients among emergency encounters within each hospital/year group.

runs.sql:
SELECT e.encounter_id AS unit_id,
       p.patient_id,
       e.data_holder AS g0,
       CAST(year(e.start_date) AS VARCHAR) AS g1,
       TRUE AS m0_in,
       TRUE AS m1_in
FROM encounters e JOIN patients p ON p.patient_id = e.patient_id
WHERE (e.type IN ('emergency')) AND (e.start_date >= DATE '2023-01-01') AND (e.start_date <= DATE '2025-12-31')

assessment.justification: Request is for aggregate counts per region of heart failure patients aged 50-80 to inform trial site selection; this is a 'health data request' for anonymised statistics only.
assessment.explanation_for_applicant: Your purpose of assessing feasibility for a clinical trial by region falls under scientific research, which is allowed under Art. 53. However, since you are requesting anonymised aggregate statistics (counts per region), this can be fully answered without individual-level records, so it is processed as a standard statistics request rather than a record-level data request.

notes: Heart failure defined as ICD-10 starting with I50 per definitions.

runs.sql:
SELECT p.patient_id AS unit_id,
       p.patient_id,
       p.region AS g0,
       TRUE AS m0_in
FROM patients p
WHERE (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conditions c WHERE (c.patient_id = p.patient_id) AND ((c.icd10 LIKE 'I50%')))) AND ((p.age >= 50) AND (p.age <= 80))

runs.sql:
SELECT p.patient_id AS unit_id,
       p.patient_id,
       p.sex AS g0,
       CASE WHEN p.age >= 0 AND p.age <= 39 THEN '0-39' WHEN p.age >= 40 AND p.age <= 59 THEN '40-59' WHEN p.age >= 60 AND p.age <= 79 THEN '60-79' WHEN p.age >= 80 THEN '80+' END AS g1,

FROM patients p
